members.name: persuasion_v5
members.instructions: {"task": "Tag the final persuader message ('Persuader message to tag') in a charity-donation chat with the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses. The persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate to Save the Children.", "notes": ["Tag only the final persuader message; use the earlier lines (which may be partly out of order) only as context.", "If a message does several things, pick its main act.", "Almost any statement about the charity itself is credibility-appeal.", "'Even a small amount helps' messages are foot-in-the-door rather than logical-appeal."]}

criteria.greeting: Opening hello or the how-are-you exchange, including the persuader's reply inside it ('Hi!', 'Hello there!', 'How are you today?', 'I'm good how are you?', 'Glad you are doing well', 'Doing alright').
criteria.closing: Closing or farewell wish at the end of the chat that does not thank ('Have a great day!', 'Have a great night!', 'I hope you enjoy the rest of your day').
criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee ('Thank you so much', 'thank you for your time and donation', 'We appreciate your help'), including a thanks right after they pledge.
criteria.praise-user: Compliments the persuadee personally or their decision/generosity ('That's awesome and generous!', 'People like you make the world better', 'you are a very kind person'), and a generic 'Great!'/'That's great!' right after the persuadee agrees to donate.
criteria.acknowledgement: Agrees with or reacts to the content of what the persuadee just said ('I agree.', 'that's true', 'That's great to hear', 'Ok, I understand that', 'Me too.', 'Absolutely.' agreeing with a statement, 'I know it is hard to trust people'), including a generic 'Great!' reacting to news or an opinion.
criteria.filler: Flat filler or a bare answer with no content: 'Ok...', 'Fine...', 'yeah..', 'yes, indeed', or a bare 'Yes'/'I have' answering the persuadee's question; confirming the donation amount ('So you are donating $10, right?'); anything conversational that fits no other option.
criteria.answer-about-self: The persuader gives a plain factual answer to a question the persuadee just asked about the persuader, with no persuasive content and no statement that the persuader gives: where they live, what their job is, that they have not donated or are not familiar ('I live in Florida.', 'I work with children of abuse.', 'No, honestly I don't', 'Yes, I am familiar with them.'). If the persuader says they donate, have donated or will donate, use self-modeling instead; if the answer argues for donating, use that appeal.
criteria.off-task: Chit-chat unrelated to the charity or donating: the persuader's location, weather, the HIT/survey mechanics unrelated to the donation, jokes, unrelated personal remarks ('North Carolina is nice', 'we need 10 chats each to complete this hit'), when not answering a question the persuadee asked.
criteria.credibility-appeal: Any statement about Save the Children itself: naming or introducing it, what it is and does, where it works, its programs, history, founder, reputation, celebrities, finances ('86% goes to programs'), website links or 'URL', answers to 'what do they do?', praising the organization ('it is a trustable fund', 'They are very renowned').
criteria.emotion-appeal: Describes children's suffering or tries to make the persuadee feel sad, guilty, hopeful or moved: grim statistics about children dying or being killed, vivid descriptions of poverty or war, third-person stories about a specific child (e.g. the story of Bruce), including sentences of such a story that mention Save the Children, expressing the persuader's own feelings about the children ('It makes me so sad'), 'the children need you'.
criteria.logical-appeal: Reasoning about why giving makes sense or makes a difference: what a donation achieves ('Your donation could help many young children', 'Donations make a huge difference'), moral reasoning ('children are the future', 'everyone deserves a chance', 'we should all pitch in'), comparisons of spending.
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Stresses that even a small amount helps or asks for a small amount first: 'every little bit helps', 'even 10 cents makes a difference', 'could you afford maybe fifteen cents?', 'pocket change', 'any amount would help'.
criteria.self-modeling: The persuader states their own donating behaviour or intention, as a model to follow: 'I will also give money today', 'I donate to them regularly', 'I'll match your donation', 'I gave what was given to me', 'I give $30 a month', 'I have in the past', including when answering the persuadee's question about whether the persuader donates.
criteria.personal-story: The persuader narrates their own personal experience related to the cause: 'I worked in Africa and saw the difference a few dollars makes', 'I have been to poor countries', 'I have worked with some charities in the past'.
criteria.donation-information: Explains the donation procedure: amount range ($0 to $2 / all of your payment), deducted from the task payment, the research team collects and sends it, how or where to donate, matching or doubling schemes.
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee knows or has heard of Save the Children or what they know about it ('Are you familiar with Save the Children?', 'Have you heard of them?').
criteria.task-related-inquiry: Asks the persuadee's opinion or an open question about donating, the charity, the cause or the conversation ('What do you think of it?', 'Do you believe children in need deserve help?', 'What is the best way to help the kids?', 'Is this something you care about?', 'Any questions?'). Not questions about the persuadee's own donating or volunteering history, and not questions asking whether they would be interested or willing to donate (those are proposition-of-donation).
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life and personal experience, including their own donating and volunteering history and habits: 'Do you have children?', 'Where are you from?', 'Do you donate to charities?', 'Have you ever donated before?', 'Which charities do you give to?', 'Do you volunteer?', 'Have you ever thought about volunteering?'.
criteria.proposition-of-donation: Asks or urges the persuadee to donate, without asking for an amount: 'Would you be willing to donate some of your payment?', 'Would you consider donating?', 'We should donate to them!', 'Donate some money maybe?', 'Would you be interested in that?' when 'that' is donating.
criteria.ask-donation-amount: Asks how much the persuadee will donate, or proposes a specific amount: 'How much would you like to give?', 'What amount would you feel comfortable donating?', 'May I suggest $.50 or even $1?'.

members.instructions: {"role": "You annotate persuader turns in chats where a persuader asks a crowd worker to give part of their task payment to Save the Children.", "question": "Which strategy or dialogue act does the last line, 'Persuader message to tag', perform?", "guidance": ["Earlier lines are context only and may be out of order.", "Choose the single main act.", "Statements about the charity itself default to credibility-appeal.", "'Even a little helps' is foot-in-the-door."]}

criteria.closing: {"definition": "A goodbye or good wish at the end of the chat, without thanks.", "examples": ["Have a great night!", "Take care have a great day."]}
criteria.thank: {"definition": "Expresses gratitude to the persuadee, e.g. for their time or their pledge.", "examples": ["Thank you very much.", "We appreciate your help in Saving the Children!"]}
criteria.praise-user: {"definition": "Praises the persuadee as a person or praises their decision; a bare 'Great!' immediately after they agree to give.", "examples": ["That's awesome and generous!", "you are an excellent human being"]}
criteria.acknowledgement: {"definition": "Shows agreement, understanding or a reaction to the content of the persuadee's last remark; a bare 'Great!' reacting to news or an opinion.", "examples": ["I agree.", "That's great to hear.", "I understand financial strain", "Me too."]}
criteria.filler: {"definition": "Contentless filler, a bare yes/no answer to a persuadee question, a check of the pledged amount, or any conversational line that has no other option.", "examples": ["Ok...", "yah?", "So you are donating $10 to Save the Children, right?", "sorry, i meant URL"]}

criteria.emotion-appeal: {"definition": "Appeals to feelings: suffering of children, grim statistics, vivid hardship, a narrative about a particular child such as Bruce (even if it names the charity), the persuader's own sadness, 'the children need you'.", "examples": ["In countries like Syria, 1000 children have been killed during the civil war.", "It makes me so sad...", "Some of them are basically naked and have nothing."]}
criteria.logical-appeal: {"definition": "Argues with reasons: what donations accomplish, moral reasoning, comparisons of what money buys.", "examples": ["Donations made from people like you can directly improve the lives of thousands of children.", "children are the future", "we should all pitch in"]}
criteria.foot-in-the-door: {"definition": "Says a tiny amount still counts, or asks for a small amount to start.", "examples": ["every little bit helps", "Even 10 cents makes a difference", "could you afford maybe fifteen cents?"]}
criteria.self-modeling: {"definition": "The persuader reports their own giving, now, past or planned, as an example to follow, including when answering 'do you donate?'.", "examples": ["I will also give money today.", "I give $30 a month", "I have in the past.", "I'll match your donation"]}
criteria.personal-story: {"definition": "The persuader tells about their own experiences connected to helping or poverty.", "examples": ["I worked in Africa earlier this year and saw the difference a few dollars can make.", "I'm back in the UK now - I was in South Africa for work."]}
criteria.donation-information: {"definition": "Explains how the donation works: range from $0 to the full payment, deduction from task payment, the research team forwarding it, ways or places to give.", "examples": ["Your donation will be directly deducted from your task payment.", "The research team will collect all donations and send it to Save the Children."]}
criteria.source-related-inquiry: {"definition": "Asks whether the persuadee knows of Save the Children or what they know about it.", "examples": ["Have you heard of them?", "Are you familiar with the organization?"]}
criteria.task-related-inquiry: {"definition": "Asks for the persuadee's opinion or an open question on donating, the charity, the cause or the chat; not their own donation history and not whether they would donate.", "examples": ["What do you think of it?", "what are your thoughts about child abuse?", "Any questions?"]}
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: {"definition": "Asks about the persuadee's own life, including their own donating or volunteering history.", "examples": ["Do you have children?", "Where are you from?", "Do you usually donate to charities?", "Have you ever volunteered?"]}
criteria.proposition-of-donation: {"definition": "Asks or urges the persuadee to give, without asking for an amount; includes asking if they would be interested or willing to donate.", "examples": ["Would you be willing to donate some of your task payment?", "We should donate to them!", "Would you be interested in that?"]}
criteria.ask-donation-amount: {"definition": "Asks how much they will give, or names a specific amount to give.", "examples": ["How much would you like to give?", "May I suggest $.50 or even $1 if you are able?"]}
